I think it is better to just use the name of the directory the lib came from. This way it is more likely to work if this gets deployed on a weird distro that puts libs in an extra directory like debian/ubuntu but doesn't have `-linux-gnu`. 

I originally was going to always add the `$(uname -m)-linux-gnu` symlink regardless if it was needed or not, if it wasn't needed it wasn't going to hurt anything. 

But now that I added some logic, better use the name of the parent directory to make the symlink, if it doesn't match `lib` then it gets symlinked. We avoid using `uname -m` as well.
